Sources

Project basis

NYU CS6903/4783 — Project 1.3. CiGuide helps non-experts choose private-key encryption configurations using an extended lecture table, adaptive questions and a random-target correctness experiment.

Lecture slides

These are page positions in the user-provided PDFs, rather than internal lecture labels.

  • f21-cs6903-lecture5.pdf: p. 28 — CBC; p. 30 — CTR and parallel processing.
  • f21-cs6903-lecture6.pdf: p. 19 — HMAC; p. 24 — Encrypt-then-MAC; pp. 25–26 — timestamping; p. 27 — the original comparison table.

Added rows and columns

  • AES-GCM: NIST SP 800-38D — authenticated encryption, nonce limits, parallel and online processing; Appendix D covers replay limitations. GCM security analysis (CRYPTO 2016) supports the PRP-based security explanation.
  • AES-CCM: NIST SP 800-38C and RFC 3610 §6 — CTR with CBC-MAC, sequential authentication and advance message-length requirements.
  • Freshness Check: Lecture 6, pp. 25–27. Timestamp checking alone does not prevent every replay.
  • Storage and Time Complexity: project-derived analytic expressions based on the constructions above. Padding follows RFC 5652 §6.3; SHA-256/HMAC details follow RFC 6234.
  • Message Length, Integrated Authentication and Parallel Encryption: derived from CBC/HMAC and the GCM/CCM specifications above; CBC/CTR details also appear in NIST SP 800-38A.

Project choices and limits

Rows 1–3 adapt the lecture by choosing CBC, HMAC-SHA256 and PKCS#7 padding. Storage formulas count output data and listed metadata, not working memory. Time formulas are analytic, not measured speeds. Questions, IDK examples and preference ranking are project designs.

Choice correctness counts a trial as successful when the target appears anywhere in the result list; it does not guarantee a unique answer. Storage budgets remain unassessed. A finished slide deck and presentation recording are still required.

Definitions and assumptions

All lengths are in bytes: n = plaintext length; a = associated-data length; p = PKCS#7 padding (1–16 bytes for CBC); v = IV/nonce length; t = authentication-tag length; s = timestamp length. CBC IVs are 16 bytes; full HMAC-SHA256 tags are 32 bytes.

Storage counts the ciphertext and listed metadata stored with it. It excludes keys, associated data, protocol headers and replay state. Time bounds assume linear processing and fixed key/tag/timestamp sizes. If CBC configurations authenticate variable-length associated data, their bounds also become O(n + a). Parallelizability is not a measured speed ranking.

Timestamp freshness checking alone does not prevent all duplicate replays or guarantee ordering. Decrypted data must not be released before authentication succeeds. Message-length requirements describe the algorithms; library APIs may impose additional restrictions.

Ranking rules

After requirement filtering, a matching Yes preference earns one point. No and I don’t know earn none. Follow-ups compare combined protection, skipping optional timestamp checks, and parallel encryption. Only preferences that differ among eligible candidates are asked. Ties share a rank; order within a tie has no meaning. Ranking never removes eligible candidates. It is not a security-strength or measured-speed ranking.

Reproduce and interpret

Run python3 run.py evaluate. Results: reports/evaluation_results.json. Run python3 run.py build to refresh all reports, documentation and browser data together. The default experiment uniformly samples targets with seed 6903 and does not simulate IDK; IDK handling is tested separately.

Returning multiple candidates can make inclusion high. This score is not unique identification and is not directly comparable to choosing one scheme randomly. Preferences are generated from target properties, not measured from real users. Storage suitability is not assessed.
